title: pQCee Enters U.S. Public Sector Through Carahsoft Master Aggregator Agreement - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Singapore's pQCee has signed Carahsoft as its Master Government Aggregator to sell post-quantum cybersecurity software to U.S. federal, municipal, education and healthcare buyers through the TIPS and OMNIA Partners contracts. The deal is framed around compliance pressure from Executive Order 14412 and public buyers' preference for drop-in crypto-agile overlays.

insights.claim: pQCee partnered with Carahsoft, acting as Master Government Aggregator, to distribute its post-quantum encryption suites to U.S. federal, municipal, educational and healthcare buyers. Sales will go through pre-negotiated cooperative purchasing contracts (TIPS and OMNIA Partners) that bypass individual agency procurement cycles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small PQC vendors are using aggregator channels to reach U.S. government demand quickly.
